sourcedFrom: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The Ghost M really does come apart: a main tube with five full steel baffles and one short one, a module tube with three full aluminium baffles and one short one, a steel cap baffle that lives with the front cap, and a booster at the rear. Because it mixes steel and aluminium, one cleaning method is legal for half of it and forbidden for the other half. The caliber box in this manual is printed against the designation GHOST 45; that is quoted as printed rather than rewritten.

steps.title: Clear the host, and use the host's own manual
steps.action: Magazine out, slide or bolt locked back, chamber checked by eye and by finger before the can is handled. The Ghost M manual then sends you to the operator's manual for your own firearm for the clearing procedure, and rules out fitting or removing a suppressor on a closed action.
steps.prose: This can sits on pistols and subguns. Their clearing drills differ, and only the host's book has yours.
steps.quote: CHECK YOUR WEAPON'S CHAMBER AND MAKE CERTAIN THAT THE WEAPON IS UNLOADED AND THE MAGAZINE REMOVED BEFORE PROCEEDING ANY FURTHER. IF THERE IS ANY QUESTION OR DOUBT, CONSULT THE OPERATOR'S MANUAL APPLICABLE TO YOUR FIREARM AS TO THE PROPER PROCEDURE FOR CLEARING AND/OR UNLOADING YOUR WEAPON. DO NOT INSTALL YOUR NEW SUPPRESSOR ON A FIREARM WITH A CLOSED ACTION!
steps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Product Overview, p.4
steps.warn: Never mount or unmount on a closed action.

steps.title: Ceiling — 10mm or 300BLK subsonic, .45 bore
steps.action: Confirm what has been fired through it. The ceiling is 10mm or 300 BLK subsonic pressure and a .45 bore, and high pressure centrefire rifle cartridges are explicitly forbidden. Note that the manual prints this restriction against the designation GHOST 45 rather than Ghost M; it is the caliber box that governs this can.
steps.prose: 300 BLK SUBSONIC is the operative word. Supersonic 300 BLK is not what this ceiling covers.
steps.quote: OUR PRODUCTS ARE CALIBER SPECIFIC. UNLESS STATED OTHERWISE ON THE SUPPRESSOR ITSELF OR ON THE PACKAGING, THE GHOST 45 SUPPRESSOR WILL NOT FUNCTION SAFELY WITH ANY CARTRIDGE WITH PRESSURES HIGHER THAN 10MM OR 300BLK SUBSONIC OR CALIBER GREATER THAN .45. USE OF YOUR SUPPRESSOR OUTSIDE OF ITS INTENDED SCOPE COULD RESULT IN DAMAGE TO YOUR FIREARM, DAMAGE TO PROPERTY, BODILY INJURY, OR DEATH. DO NOT FIRE HIGH PRESSURE RIFLE CENTERFIRE CARTRIDGES THROUGH YOUR GHOST 45 SUPPRESSOR.
steps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Installation, p.6
steps.warn: No high pressure centrefire rifle cartridges. Ceiling 10mm / 300BLK subsonic / .45 bore.

steps.title: The barrel must give the piston a shoulder
steps.action: Check the muzzle before the can goes back on. It needs a proper shoulder to seat against or a muzzle face cut square to the bore; on a long thread the can seats on the muzzle itself and the back of the piston may never reach the shoulder.
steps.prose: A pistol thread cut slightly off-axis will still let the can spin on happily and still walk the group.
steps.caution: No square shoulder or muzzle face, no mount.
steps.quote: DO NOT thread onto barrels that don't have a proper shoulder to seat against, or muzzle face that is not cut square to the bore.
steps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Installation, Step One, p.5

steps.title: Take the Ghost M off the host
steps.action: With the can cool enough to hold, rotate the body or end cap counter-clockwise until it starts to unthread from the muzzle, or clockwise if you are running a left-hand metric piston or mount. Grip the body, not the front cap — pulling on the cap unscrews the can into pieces instead of off the barrel.
steps.prose: The tube and the module thread together, so anything you turn at the front is a joint you did not mean to open.
steps.quote: To remove the suppressor simply rotate the body / end cap of the suppressor counterclockwise until it begins to unthread from the muzzle of the host weapon. If a left hand metric piston/ mount is used, then unscrew by rotating clockwise.
steps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Installation, Step Three, p.7
steps.warn: A hot can burns. Protective clothing, or let it cool.

steps.title: Booster out — and NOT back onto a fixed barrel
steps.action: Unscrew the piston retainer and take out the piston and spring. The whole booster mechanism comes out with an AR-15 castle nut wrench. If your host is a fixed-barrel firearm, the booster does not go back in — a fixed mount or 3-Lug adapter replaces it, because the booster's repeated impact will damage a firearm whose barrel does not recoil with it.
steps.prose: Whatever mount replaces it must be secured with the castle nut wrench before the can is fired.
steps.quote: Warning: Do not use the Booster Mechanism on fixed barreled firearms as the repeated impact will damage the firearm.
steps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Disassembly & Cleaning, Step One, p.9
steps.warn: Booster on a fixed-barrel host will damage the firearm.

steps.title: Module off, front cap off
steps.action: Unscrew the module from the main body by turning counter-clockwise and take the front cap off it. Both were assembled hand tight over greased threads and should break by hand; the front cap comes off with the provided tool and brings the steel cap baffle with it.
steps.prose: That cap baffle is not optional hardware — track where it goes, because the reassembly rule below is built on it.
steps.quote: STEP TWO: REMOVE MODULE Unscrew Module from the main body by turning counter-clockwise and remove Front Cap.
steps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Disassembly & Cleaning, Step Two, p.9

steps.title: Steel baffles out of the main tube
steps.action: With the module tube off, push the baffles out of the BACK of the main tube — the end the booster screwed into — having first removed the piston or the whole booster so there is a clear path. A 5/8 inch wooden dowel and light taps with a hammer will move them if they are stuck. Expect five full steel baffles and one short steel baffle.
steps.prose: Wooden, so nothing harder than the baffles touches the bore of the tube. Count them out; the short one is always last in its set.
steps.quote: MAIN TUBE: With the module tube removed, push out the baffles from the back of the suppressor where the Booster screwed in. Ensure the piston or the whole booster mechanism is removed to facilitate easily pushing the baffles out. A 5/8" wooden dowel and hammer can be used to gently tap the baffles out of the tube. The Main Tube contains five (5) full steel baffles and one (1) short steel baffle.
steps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Disassembly & Cleaning, Step Two, p.9

steps.title: Aluminium baffles out of the module tube
steps.action: Use the provided tool to take the front cap off the module along with the steel cap baffle, then push on the exposed baffle at the back of the module to slide the stack out the front. Expect three full aluminium baffles and one short aluminium baffle. Keep these separate from the steel set — the cleaning rules differ.
steps.prose: Nine baffles plus the cap baffle in total. Lay the two sets out in their own rows.
steps.quote: MODULE TUBE: Use the provided tool to remove the front Cap along with the steel Cap Baffle. Push on the exposed baffle at the back of the module to slide the baffles out the front of the tube. The Module Tube contains three (3) full aluminum baffles and one (1) short aluminum baffle.
steps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Disassembly & Cleaning, Step Two, p.9

steps.title: NO aluminium and NO tube in the peroxide/vinegar dip
steps.action: If you use the hydrogen peroxide and vinegar dip that is common practice for .22 fouling, keep the aluminium baffles, the aluminium front cap and the tube itself out of it. Dead Air states this outright. Aluminium in that bath does not just discolour, it is attacked.
steps.prose: The dip is also a health hazard in its own right — dissolved lead, eye protection, nitrile gloves, and proper disposal under local rules.
steps.quote: NOTE: DO NOT PLACE ANY ALUMINUM COMPONENTS OR THE TUBE ITSELF INTO THE “DIP”.
steps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Installation — Solvents and Lead Exposure, p.5
steps.warn: Unprotected exposure to the dip can cause serious health issues including lead poisoning.

steps.title: Wet firing — the manufacturer's own procedure
steps.action: Shooting the Ghost M wet is explicitly permitted and has a published dose: a water bottle capful, or 3 to 5 CCs of water, poured down the piston and into the booster mechanism, then mount to the pistol and fire a magazine or two through it. It softens carbon in the piston so it wipes out afterwards.
steps.prose: This is a booster-configuration procedure, so it inherits the fixed-barrel prohibition above. Do it on a tilting-barrel host only.
steps.quote: To shoot the suppressor wet, pour a water bottle capful (or 3-5 CCs of water) down the piston and into the booster mechanism, mount to pistol, and shoot a magazine or two ammo through it.
steps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Disassembly & Cleaning, p.8

steps.title: WIPES — never with the optional short caps
steps.action: If you run a wipe, it goes in the wipe front cap only. Dead Air forbids using the wipe with the optional short caps, because doing so may damage the cap. Push the wipe straight into the back of the wipe cap so it seats on the shoulder just inside — if it has a tapered cut edge, that edge goes in first — and always tighten the wipe cap with the provided tool so the wipe is fully captured.
steps.prose: A wipe pushed too far, onto the inside face of the cap, is past where it belongs, and a bullet through the cap will damage it.
steps.quote: NEVER USE THE WIPE WITH OUR OPTIONAL “SHORT” CAPS. DOING SO MAY CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE CAP.
steps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Reassembly — Wipes, p.11

steps.title: No homemade wipes
steps.action: Do not cut your own wipe for the Ghost M. Dead Air rules homemade wipes out because they may come loose in the suppressor and damage it — a wipe that migrates is a piece of rubber loose in the bore path of a can you are firing through.
steps.prose: That is a different rule from the Wolfman's, where Dead Air does describe sourcing your own rubber. Two models, two positions; use the one printed for the can in your hand.
steps.quote: DO NOT USE HOMEMADE WIPES IN THE SUPPRESSOR AS THEY MAY COME LOOSE AND DAMAGE THE SUPPRESSOR.
steps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Reassembly — Wipes, p.11

steps.title: THE CAP BAFFLE ALWAYS GOES BACK
steps.action: The steel cap baffle travels with the front cap — the wipe front cap or either optional short cap, no exceptions. If the can is assembled without it, the baffle stack is not secured, and Dead Air states that firing it in that state will damage the suppressor. Physically account for the cap baffle before the cap is tightened.
steps.prose: It is easy to lose because it comes off attached to the cap and looks like part of it. Check for it every single time.
steps.quote: WARNING:  THE CAP BAFFLE ALWAYS TRAVELS WITH THE FRONT CAP, WHETHER IT’S THE WIPE FRONT CAP OR ONE OF THE OPTIONAL SHORT FRONT CAPS. ASSEMBLING THE SUPPRESSOR WITHOUT IT WILL NOT SECURE THE BAFFLES AND IT WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO YOUR SUPPRESSOR WHEN YOU SHOOT IT.
steps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Reassembly, p.12
steps.warn: No cap baffle means the baffles are not secured. Do not fire it.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You should have the booster stripped, the module off the main body, the front cap and its steel cap baffle off, six steel baffles out of the main tube and four aluminium baffles out of the module — and you have the wipe and cap-baffle rules in hand for the rebuild. Deep Clean covers baffle separation, the two cleaning chemistries and the stacking order.
steps.prose: The routine interval on the baffles is about 1000 rounds depending on ammunition; the booster is every session.
steps.quote: Depending on the type of ammunition that you use, your suppressor should not require disassembly and cleaning of the baffles for up to 1000 rounds.
steps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Disassembly & Cleaning, p.8

deepSteps.title: Separating baffles without damaging them
deepSteps.action: Most of the time a slight wiggle as you pull two baffles apart is enough — only a small amount of separation is needed before they break loose entirely. Where carbon has locked them, insert a screwdriver blade into the shallow tool slot on the side of the baffle and twist; the baffle only needs to move a little, and it can be tilted so the inner cone clears deposits.
deepSteps.prose: Pry in the tool slot, never on the baffle rim. A bent rim will not seat and then the whole stack sits proud.
deepSteps.quote: If the baffles are tight, then a screw driver can be used to lightly pry them apart. Simply insert the blade of the screw driver into the shallow tool slot on the side of the baffles and twist.
deepSteps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Disassembly & Cleaning, Step Three, p.9

deepSteps.title: Steel one way, aluminium another
deepSteps.action: The stainless baffles from the main body can be cleaned the same way as the booster — including submersion in carbon scrubbing chemicals. The aluminium baffles and front cap from the module tube usually need almost nothing for thousands of rounds, and when they do, only mild chemicals friendly to anodised aluminium.
deepSteps.prose: Two materials, two chemistries. That is the whole reason the two baffle sets should never be cleaned in one bath.
deepSteps.caution: Aluminium never goes in the dip, and never in aggressive carbon chemistry.
deepSteps.quote: The aluminum baffles and front cap found in the Module Tube should not require cleaning for thousands of rounds because of the lack of buildup that occurs in this area of the suppressor. These should be cleaned with mild chemicals that are friendly to anodized aluminum.
deepSteps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Disassembly & Cleaning, p.8

deepSteps.title: Booster service — every session
deepSteps.action: Clean the booster with its spring and piston every shooting session and inspect the O-ring. Replacements are size -018. Housing, piston and spring can also come out and be submerged in carbon scrubbing chemicals when wiping is not enough.
deepSteps.prose: This is the part of the Ghost M that decides whether a pistol keeps cycling. It fouls fastest and it is the cheapest to keep right.
deepSteps.quote: The Booster mechanism with the spring and piston should be cleaned every shooting session and the O-Ring inspected. Replacement O-Rings are size -018 and are available from Dead Air Silencers.
deepSteps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Disassembly & Cleaning, p.8

deepSteps.title: Baffle order and orientation on the way back
deepSteps.action: Align the steel baffles so all the ports face the same direction, and push each one fully into the previous with its tabs seated in the LARGEST slots. Repeat for the aluminium set. Each set ends with its own short baffle. If a tab drops into a tool slot instead of a large slot the baffle is not seated, and the tell is that the front cap or module will not tighten down as far as it should.
deepSteps.prose: Ports aligned is a performance matter; tabs in the large slots is a safety matter, because an unseated stack is a stack the cap cannot clamp.
deepSteps.quote: Align the steel baffles such that all of the ports are oriented the same direction. Ensure each baffle is fully inserted into the previous with the tabs seating into the largest slots. Repeat for the aluminum baffles. Ensure each set of baffles has the shortest baffle as the final baffle.
deepSteps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Reassembly, Step One, p.10

deepSteps.title: Reassembly check — the gap tells you if it is right
deepSteps.action: With the can back together, look at the joint on the main tube: the gap should be very narrow, under about forty thousandths. A wider gap means the baffles were not properly stacked, an alignment tab is sitting in a tool slot, or debris is stopping the baffles nesting.
deepSteps.prose: If the module tube bottoms out against the main tube, check all six main-tube baffles actually went in.
deepSteps.quote: Note Gap on main tube should be very narrow (less than .040").
deepSteps.cite: Ghost M  DEAD AIR  turn up the silence.™  OWNER'S MANUAL — Rev121323 — Reassembly, Step Four, p.12

cleaning.name: STEEL BAFFLES & MAIN TUBE
tasks: Five full steel baffles and one short steel baffle — keep the short one last in the set
Clean them as you would the booster, including carbon scrubbing chemicals if needed
Do NOT put the tube itself into the peroxide and vinegar dip

cleaning.name: ALUMINIUM BAFFLES & FRONT CAP
tasks: Three full aluminium baffles and one short aluminium baffle, plus the aluminium front cap
Mild chemicals friendly to anodised aluminium only
Never place aluminium components into the dip

cleaning.name: BOOSTER
tasks: Clean the spring and piston every shooting session and inspect the O-ring
Wipe carbon out of the booster housing with the spring and piston removed
Housing, piston and spring may be submerged in carbon scrubbing chemicals

cleaning.name: SAFETY WHILE CLEANING
tasks: Protective eyewear and nitrile gloves whenever the dip is in use
Dispose of solvent and dissolved lead in accordance with local ordinances
Wash hands and exposed skin afterwards

reassembly: Clean and lightly grease all threads and baffle contact points before anything goes back.
Align each set of baffles so the ports face the same way, seat every tab in the largest slot, and finish each set with its short baffle.
Stand the assembled main-body baffles vertically on the bench and slide the tube down over them, then tilt, push the last baffle fully in and flip the assembly.
Repeat for the module tube baffles.
Full configuration: drop the cap baffle onto the end of the aluminium stack in the module, tighten the front cap with the provided tool, then screw the module into the main body.
Short configuration: drop the cap baffle onto the end of the main-tube stack and tighten the cap into the main tube with the provided tool.
If a wipe is used, it goes only in the wipe front cap, seated on the internal shoulder, tightened with the provided tool.
fncheck: Check the gap at the main tube joint is under about .040 inch, that the front cap sits at the correct depth for the cap you fitted, and that the cap baffle is physically present. Mount the can, confirm it is straight to the bore centreline and not canted, and confirm nothing rattles before it is fired.
